the_four_verdicts.evaluation_order: INVALID first, then UNTESTED, then EVIDENCE AGAINST, then EVIDENCE OF SKILL. A cohort cannot be called skilful or wrong until it has passed both of the first two.

v0_INVALID.audited_2026_08_18_result: NOT YET RUN. The two data-shaped triggers (ts-coupling, window-coverage) cannot be verified until the grade runs at maturity, because they require the resolved snapshot grid. This standard pre-commits the trigger conditions; Part 2 of the build verifies them against the frozen freeze-time inputs.
v0_INVALID.consequence: Fix, disclose, and resolve the NEXT cohort. It does not license re-freezing the failed one.
v0_INVALID.meaning: A pipeline fault. Not a result about the model.
triggers_any_of: any row with fee_growth_anomaly > 0 (a fee_growth reset was clamped to zero, which DISCARDS real fees - economics/clmm_fee.py)
any row rejected as window_span_short or insufficient_completeness at maturity - the DATA did not span the claimed 14-day horizon even though the wall clock did (the grader's gate_4 coverage floor)

any row where the first in-window snapshot ts is not the prediction ts (entry-price coupling: the grade derives entry s0 from the first snapshot >= T; the prediction froze entry from the last snapshot <= T)

v1_UNTESTED.batch_b_is_ALREADY_IN_THE_AGAINST_BRANCH: The frozen zero-trap probability for canonical batch B is P(0 traps) = Pi(1-y_prob) = 0.0021433554373314957 <= 0.01 (the 1% level). MEASURED E = 4.7369 is a separate cross-check: it sits ABOVE even the 1% Poisson E level (4.6052). 2 of 22 rows carry y_prob >= 0.50 (max 0.5751), 9 carry y_prob exactly 0.0000. So: IF NO POOL TRAPS, THE VERDICT IS EVIDENCE AGAINST @1%, AND THAT IS FIXED NOW, BEFORE ANY OUTCOME, BY THE FROZEN PREDICTIONS ALONE. This is the mirror image of SOL batch-2, whose E=0.2886 pre-sealed UNTESTED.
binding_reporting_rules: It must NOT be reported as '22/22 correct', '100% accuracy', or any win-rate. An all-safe prediction set in an all-safe window is a null result. '22/22' converts a measurement of the window into a claim about the model.

In the zero-trap branch roc_auc, pr_auc, brier, precision, and recall are UNDEFINED in the ledger (the SUI grader's safe_* wrappers return the UNDEFINED sentinel on single-class y_true; safe_precision and safe_recall gained the _degenerate guard on 2026-08-18 to match safe_roc_auc/safe_pr_auc/safe_brier - the ledger no longer carries coerced precision=0.0/recall=0.0 floats and gate_5_degenerate no longer records a coerced-metric failure on a legitimate zero-trap ledger). Republish any of them as UNDEFINED if a downstream copy coerced them.

The BOOTSTRAP blocks: with single-class y_true the cluster and iid bootstrap paths short-circuit to UNDEFINED (degenerate guard), so no coerced bootstrap numbers reach the ledger. Verified by reading the guard; re-verify on the real ledger.

What MAY be claimed: the pipeline resolved end to end (freeze -> maturity -> grade -> hash-signed ledger -> publication); the maturity and completeness/coverage gates fired as specified; realized_net was computable from real on-chain fee_growth deltas; and the interval-coverage count, which is a real measurement.
v1_UNTESTED.trigger: E = sum(y_prob) over the cohort < 3.3 AND realized trap count == 0. E is computable before any outcome. This is the ONLY place E appears as a boundary: E<3.3 is the UNTESTED gate's form, and NOTHING ELSE. The v2 zero_trap_contradiction does NOT use E - it uses the exact P(0 traps)=Pi(1-y_prob) product at named 5%/1% levels, which is the sharper quantity (for batch B P(0)=0.0021 bounds E tighter than any E-threshold can).
v1_UNTESTED.why_3_3_and_not_3_45: SOL used 3.45 = 23 x 0.15, the common-p row where (1-p)^n first drops below ~5%. That constant is n-specific. RECOMPUTED for n=22: the same construction gives 22 x 0.15 = 3.3, where (0.85)^22 = 0.0280 (SOL's (0.85)^23 = 0.024). 3.3 sits between the Poisson 5% and 1% E levels (2.9957 and 4.6052), matching SOL's placement of 3.45 between exp(-3.45)=0.032 and the 5%/1% levels. This constant governs ONLY the UNTESTED gate. It is NOT a zero_trap_contradiction boundary: the contradiction trigger is the exact product, below.

v2_EVIDENCE_AGAINST.meaning: The model is wrong, not merely unlucky. Any ONE trigger suffices.
v2_EVIDENCE_AGAINST.the_grader_does_not_compute_the_primary_: sui_grade.py stores prediction_lower/prediction_upper in every ledger row and computes interval COVERAGE only in the sense of observed-span vs claimed horizon (gate_4). It does not count how many realized_net_return_window values fall OUTSIDE the stored prediction interval - the calibration-coverage count. Coverage will be computed off-grader from fields the ledger already contains (the same discipline as SOL), so no code change is needed to honour this standard. The SOL harness pattern carries over to a SUI coverage check.

triggers.directional_failure: mean realized_net of the top-y_prob third is ABOVE that of the bottom third - the rank signal is inverted. With n=22 the thirds are 7/8/7 rows.
triggers.interval_coverage_primary: >= 6 of 22 rows with realized_net_return_window outside [prediction_lower, prediction_upper]. RECOMPUTED for n=22: P(X>=6 | Bin(22,0.10)) = 0.0182, so this is the 5% level. (SOL's k=6 carried P=0.0226 on n=23; do not carry that tail probability forward.)
triggers.interval_coverage_strong: >= 7 misses. P(X>=7 | Bin(22,0.10)) = 0.0044, the 1% level. (SOL's k=7 carried P=0.0058 on n=23.)
triggers.miss_asymmetry: all coverage misses fall on the same side of the interval (>= 3 misses) - the interval is biased, not merely mis-scaled.
triggers.missed_trap_contradiction: any row with y_prob < 0.01 realized as a trap - the model assigned under 1% to something that happened. 9 of 22 batch-B rows carry y_prob < 0.01 (all exactly 0.0000), so this trigger is live for batch B.
triggers.zero_trap_contradiction: realized traps == 0 AND the exact zero-trap probability P(0 traps) = Pi(1 - y_prob) over the frozen y-vector is at or below a NAMED level. Levels: P(0 traps) <= 0.05 (the 5% level); P(0 traps) <= 0.01 (the 1% level, EVIDENCE AGAINST @1%). Computed from the frozen y-vector, not from E, and recomputed at grade time from the same published y_prob values. For batch B the frozen value is P(0 traps) = 0.0021433554373314957 <= 0.01, so IF NOTHING TRAPS THE VERDICT IS EVIDENCE AGAINST @1% - fixed now, before any outcome, by the frozen predictions alone.

v3_EVIDENCE_OF_SKILL.ceiling_on_the_claim: A single cohort satisfying all four is evidence of skill and nothing stronger. It is not a validated model, not a track record, and not grounds for a performance claim.
requires_all_four: The cohort was capable of being wrong: the exact zero-trap probability P(0 traps) = Pi(1-y_prob) <= 0.05 (the all-safe outcome is at most a 5% event), OR at least one realized trap. Either the prediction set was falsifiable a priori, or the window proved it was. Batch B passes this limb at P(0 traps) = 0.002143 <= 0.01. (E appears nowhere as a boundary outside the UNTESTED gate.)
realized trap count inside the central 90% of PoissonBinomial(y_prob_1..22)

interval coverage misses in {1,2,3,4,5}. ZERO misses is NOT evidence of skill: it is consistent with an over-wide interval, P(X=0) = 0.0985 (recomputed for n=22; SOL's P(X=0)=0.0886 was n=23), and with the same benign window as UNTESTED.
mean realized_net of the top-y_prob third BELOW that of the bottom third - the ordering carried information

the_one_line_commitment: If, on 2026-08-27, the 22 batch-B predictions produce zero realized traps, we will publish that as EVIDENCE AGAINST @1% the model - the zero_trap_contradiction: P(0 traps) = Pi(1-y_prob) over the frozen y-vector = 0.0021433554373314957, i.e. zero traps is a 0.21% event under the model, below the 1% level -> EVIDENCE AGAINST @1% - together with the interval-coverage count, and the statement that roc_auc/pr_auc/brier and precision/recall are UNDEFINED in the zero-trap ledger (the grader's safe_* wrappers return the UNDEFINED sentinel on single-class y_true; safe_precision/safe_recall gained the degenerate guard on 2026-08-18). We will not report it as 22/22. If any pool traps, the verdict is decided by the triggers in v2, and in particular a row with y_prob < 0.01 that traps is EVIDENCE AGAINST outright.

what_the_prediction_claims.falsifiability: A single y_prob is not falsified by a single outcome. y_pred = 1[y_prob >= 0.50] is falsifiable per row; 2 of 22 batch-B rows carry y_prob >= 0.50, so precision and recall are STRUCTURALLY DEFINED for this cohort only if at least one pool traps - if zero pools trap, y_true is single-class and precision/recall are undefined, not merely zero.
what_the_prediction_claims.in_words: The probability that a unit-native-liquidity CLMM position spanning this pool's frozen band, entered at T and held passively for 14 days, ends more than 5% below simply holding the entry basket (realized net in the USDC numeraire). No rebalancing, no gas, no compounding; fees credited only while tick_current is inside the band.
what_the_prediction_claims.the_interval: prediction_lower / prediction_upper are the 5th and 95th percentiles of the SAME 10000 realized_net values that y_prob thresholds (INTERVAL_ALPHA 0.10 -> nominal-90% interval). Same quantity, same distribution. This is the only component of a single prediction that one outcome can falsify.
what_the_prediction_claims.trap_definition_verbatim: A realized trap is y_true == 1, i.e. realized net < -0.05 (eval_net_threshold, SV7 / R2). It is NOT an interval breach. An interval breach is realized net outside [prediction_lower, prediction_upper] - a different event on a different boundary. Any tooling, report, or board that labels an interval breach as a trap is wrong and must be corrected to the same wording as the SOL harness: trap = y_true, realized < -0.05.
what_the_prediction_claims.y_prob_as_implemented: y_prob = mean over N_SIMS=10000 driftless-GBM paths of 1[realized_net_i < eval_net_threshold], with eval_net_threshold = -0.05 frozen per row (DEFAULT_TRAP_NET_RETURN_THRESHOLD in sui/protocol.py, SV7 / R2), horizon 14 days from the freeze instant T. At freeze time the score is PRICE-ONLY: realized_net_i = terminal_i / entry_price - 1. The grade later adds the realized fee side, so y_true at resolution is 1[il_component + fee_component < -0.05]. Source: sui/forecast/run_forecast.py.
